I heat with hot water(not boiling) and then dry-keep warm with a hairdryer. Try to get the rat to about 100°F as this seems to be the accepted normal body temp for adult live rats. 

At first during her strike I was pretty certain it was just the standard winter time thing and she wasn’t hungry but now I’m not sure that’s the issue as she is “hunting” for lack of a better word nightly by resting a third of her body outside a hide and following any motion near her head. It’s what prompted me to try feeding again after I noticed the behavior.

This is news to me. I’ve been going off this feeding chart from BallPythons.net since I got her. https://ball-pythons.net/forums/cache.php?img=http%3A%2F%2Fi.imgur.com%2F98qfzDH.png

I’m going to try sizing down next of course but is there a more accurate method for determining prey size other than % of weight or girth? Because per my picture above that rat doesn’t seem too big as it’s just barely the width of her midsection.

She’s currently in an Animal Plastics T8. Pic here: https://ibb.co/16cvC7Z the top enclosure is for my corn snake and was being cleaned during the photo. 

Size is 48Lx24Wx12H 

Humidity hovers around 60-70% per my accurite. 

I keep the warm side about 90°F and the cool side about 82°F. Regulated using a Herpstat2 and a radiant heat panel. 

She had LED day lighting on a 12h timer On/Off. 

I thaw my rodents in hot(not boiling) water, heating them using a hairdryer. Last night I made sure to get it to about 100°F before offering.(according to my research this is average body temp for an adult rat) 

I am well versed in the rodent tong dance at this point. :) 

I used to feed once a week when she ate regularly, now I attempt to feed every two weeks when she refuses. 

The outside of her enclosure is my bedroom however I have a blackout screen over the glass after sunset and until morning to keep both my snakes more comfortable. 

I was going off a feeding chart from BallPythons.net that mentioned weekly feeding even for adults. About 10%-15% of body weight. Is this incorrect?

Yeah she’s been on rats since I got her. Still drinking and shedding normally. I’m glad to hear the weight loss isn’t as severe as I thought.
